subject: SSO & Service Account Enablement — Cardinal access blueprint
body:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardinalhealth.com>, IT Ops <it-ops@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SSO & Service Account Enablement — Cardinal access blueprint

Hi Jordan / Cardinal team,

Great to meet you on the call last week. Per our discussion, I’m proposing a short kickoff to align on the access enablement plan for Cardinal Health’s Redwood deployment. The core scope we’ll cover on the kickoff and subsequent implementation sprint: 

- SAML/SSO metadata exchange and attribute mapping (NameID, email, groups)
- SCIM provisioning for users + group sync (delta vs full sync expectations)
- IP allowlist boundaries (production / admin / console) and expected source ranges
- Service account patterns (naming, least privilege roles, rotation)
- Org policies and logging/retention expectations (audit log export cadence)

I’ve attached an initial checklist (redwood-access-checklist.xlsx) and your SAML metadata stub (cardinal_saml_metadata.xml) — please confirm whether the metadata.xml is the latest.

Action items for kickoff: please confirm (1) which IdP (Okta/Azure AD/Other) you will use for SAML, (2) a primary and backup contact for SCIM provisioning, and (3) any IP ranges that need immediate whitelisting. Proposed kickoff window: Wed 8/12 10–11am PT or Thu 8/13 1–2pm PT.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Ops <it-ops@cardinalhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: SSO & Service Account Enablement — Cardinal access blueprint

Thanks Markus — this looks good. A few clarifying points before kickoff:

1) We are on Okta (Universal Directory) in production and currently push groups via SCIM to a few SaaS apps. We plan to enable group provisioning for Redwood but need to understand group-to-role mapping (SCIM group membership -> Redwood roles).
2) For SAML, our metadata is maintained in the team repo; attaching an updated metadata.xml (see attachment). Please confirm the expected NameID format (email vs persistent).
3) IP allowlisting: our egress is NATed; I’ll need to confirm the public ranges. For the admin console, we’d prefer a static allowlist and separate access for SRE.

Available for Wed 8/12 10–11am PT.

Jordan Price
Senior Security Engineer
Cardinal Health

Attachments: cardinal_saml_metadata_v20260810.xml

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardinalhealth.com>, IT Ops <it-ops@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSO & Service Account Enablement — Cardinal access blueprint

Jordan — thanks for the details. A few notes on the mapping and plan: 

- NameID: Redwood supports both email and persistent NameID. For group-based RBAC we recommend using SCIM groups mapped to Redwood roles (e.g., cardinal_sre -> role:infrastructure-admin).
- SCIM: we do delta syncs every 5 minutes by default; we can change to 1m if you need faster provisioning but that increases API usage. We will provide a service account for SCIM with scoped token limited to /Users and /Groups endpoints.
- Service account naming convention (proposed): redwood-scim-cardinal-<env>-svc (e.g., redwood-scim-cardinal-prod-svc). Rotation: 90 days by default; we support KMS-backed rotation if you want automated keys.
- IP allowlist tiers: 
  * Console (admin): single static CIDR block per environment
  * API (inference): regional egress ranges, optional private VPC peering for strict isolation
  * SCIM webhook endpoints: allow Cardinal IPs or require TLS client certs (we support mutual TLS)

I’ve updated the checklist in Drive (link below) with a recommended attribute map and a sample SCIM scope policy. For the kickoff we’ll walk through the mutual action plan and gather your asset owners.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-cardinal-access
HubSpot: 4738291

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-access-checklist.xlsx (updated v2)

Quick note — confirmed Wed 8/12 10–11am PT on our side; I’ll send a calendar invite with Zoom. Agenda will be: kickoff goals (10m), SAML metadata + attribute map (15m), SCIM provisioning flow (15m), service account & IP allowlist details (10m), open items & next steps (10m).

I’ll also include the link to our MSA and the current redlines (msa_redlines_v2.pdf) for legal to review in parallel — if Cardinal can point your procurement contact we can accelerate the standard T&Cs.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SSO & Service Account Enablement — Cardinal access blueprint

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick sync. Recap and immediate next steps: 

1) Kickoff confirmed: Wed 8/12 10–11am PT (Zoom invite sent by Ben).
2) Jordan to confirm IdP NameID preference (email vs persistent) during the meeting.
3) Cardinal to attach final public egress ranges and procurement contact for MSA review (we’ll circulate the redlines PDF).
4) Redwood will: 
   - Provision a scoped SCIM service account (redwood-scim-cardinal-prod-svc) and share the token with your SCIM admin via secure transfer
   - Share attribute mapping template (pre-filled) and sample role mappings
   - Provide an IP allowlist proposal for console vs API endpoints and options for private peering

Please reply if any of the above is incorrect or you want a longer kickoff agenda. Looking forward to getting this into an implementation sprint next week.

Best,
Markus
